kernel_binding.historical_build_status_meaning: Status written on the kernel-003 manifest at build time and copied into the desktop build record. It is not the runtime status. Desktop attempt-001 booted KC 7335c418, which embeds that standalone kernel. The standalone hash and the KC hash differ because they are different files.

source_facts: libmalloc vm.c mvm_protect, in both puredarwin-baseline and puredarwin-m1-desktop, calls mprotect on round_page_quanta(address+size) for the postlude and, on any nonzero result, prints the unrounded address+size with the protection argument. The prelude print is the prelude address. magazine_large.c has a separate string, 'new postlude', and prints 0x0.
round_page_quanta is round_page, which uses vm_page_size. large_vm_page_quanta_size is the larger of vm_kernel_page_size and vm_page_size (libmalloc src/base.h).

rack_init always allocates the magazine array with MALLOC_ADD_GUARD_PAGE_FLAGS|DISABLE_ASLR (magazine_rack.c). That call does not depend on MallocGuardEdges. The LP64 default in set_flags_from_environment is only MALLOC_ABORT_ON_CORRUPTION. MallocGuardEdges adds guards for large or all regions when the environment sets it.

magazine_t is 2560 bytes on the LP64 static assert. num_magazines is 1 when max magazines is not greater than 1, and the array includes the depot, so the rounded length is round_page of sizeof(magazine_t) times (num_magazines+1). logical_ncpus is read from the commpage in malloc.c. The cpus=1 bootarg is not that read.

libsystem_kernel is built with NO_SYSCALL_LEGACY. The legacy mprotect wrapper, which aligns down by PAGE_MASK, is compiled only if that macro is absent. Platforms/MacOSX/arm64/syscall.map binds _mprotect to ___mprotect.

BSD mprotect_sanitize uses VM_SANITIZE_FLAGS_CHECK_ALIGNED_START and SIZE_ZERO_FALLTHROUGH against the task map page (kern_mman.c). An unaligned start becomes KERN_INVALID_ARGUMENT and then EINVAL. KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS becomes ENOMEM. KERN_PROTECTION_FAILURE becomes EACCES. The libmalloc warning does not print errno or the kern_return.

vm_map_protect_sanitize passes only VM_SANITIZE_FLAGS_SIZE_ZERO_SUCCEEDS (vm_map.c). Without CHECK_ALIGNED_START, vm_sanitize_addr_size truncates the start and rounds the end. ANYWHERE mach_vm_map uses vm_sanitize_size without CHECK_ALIGNED_SIZE, and that helper rounds the size up to the map page.

pexpert arm64 board_config.h includes H13.h for ARM64_BOARD_CONFIG_T8103. H13.h defines __ARM_16K_PG__ 1 and __ARM_MIXED_PAGE_SIZE__ 1. Under __ARM_16K_PG__, mach_loader.c gives a 64-bit user map SIXTEENK_PAGE_SHIFT unless PMAP_CREATE_FORCE_4K_PAGES is set. That source is the kernel-003 tree whose standalone kernel.debug.t8103 (58da6e524cd3d6100129ffb04281c5413cee8582c0c93a0f2c545dfd7d741909) the desktop build record embeds in booted KC 7335c418494241a7c805d61172dcb690115dd61b6b57e833f883cdd6856f5c06.

osfmk/arm/commpage/commpage.c writes KERNEL_PAGE_SHIFT from page_shift. Under __ARM_16K_PG__ it writes SIXTEENK_PAGE_SHIFT into USER_PAGE_SHIFT_64; otherwise it writes page_shift. mach_init.c, when vm_page_shift is still 0, reads USER_PAGE_SHIFT_64 on arm64 and sets vm_page_size to 1 shifted by that value. pd_libSystem_compat.c initializes vm_page_size to 4096. dyld glue.c has a separate vm_page_size initialized to 0x1000 in dyld's image. Which process copy is live after link was not resolved.

libc mach/vm_types.h typedefs vm_address_t from vm_offset_t. The arm header typedefs vm_offset_t and vm_size_t as uintptr_t when __LP64__ is set and as natural_t otherwise. mach/mach_interface.h declares vm_protect(vm_map_t, vm_address_t, vm_size_t, boolean_t, vm_prot_t). The diagnostic uses that declaration and does not add an extern.

runtime_recorded.note: The warning text matches vm.c postlude, protection argument 0. rust-hello and chonkstep-darwin both printed it, and the desktop test still recorded 127 frame callbacks. That does not identify the live page size.

inferred_not_confirmed: The printed postlude address is the unrounded user address plus the size passed to mvm_protect. With a prelude guard, that user address is the map base plus the large quantum. If the map base and the large quantum are both multiples of 16384, a residue of 8192 means the rounded magazine-array size is 8192 mod 16384.

round_page of 5120 bytes (one magazine plus the depot) and of 7680 bytes (two magazines plus the depot) is 8192 when vm_page_size is 4096 or 8192, and 16384 when vm_page_size is 16384. A 16384 result would print residue 0 if the large quantum is a multiple of 16384. The console residue therefore fits a 16K guard quantum together with a smaller user page, and does not fit both sizes being 16K for those magazine counts.

The same residue also fits an 8K user page. The arm commpage writer in this tree stores shift 14 under __ARM_16K_PG__ and otherwise page_shift. It has no store of shift 13. Which of 4096 or 8192 was live is not established. The page-size globals were not printed.

A commpage value is not established as wrong. mach_init overwrites a zero vm_page_shift from USER_PAGE_SHIFT_64. The 4096 initializer in the stub is not, by itself, the runtime value. No commpage byte was read from the guest.

Any probe with called 0. abi_truncation 1 means the Mach call was skipped because the header typedef did not round-trip. outside_region 1 means neither call was made. A skipped record has no ret and no errno.

diagnostic.guard: checked_vm_protect is the only vm_protect call. Both the subspan site and the restore site use it. The span must lie inside the one anonymous mapping. Then (uintptr_t)(vm_address_t)address must equal address and (size_t)(vm_size_t)length must equal length. Otherwise the Mach call is skipped and the record sets abi_truncation to 1 with no ret. mprotect of an in-range span still runs.
